# Mastering Quarto {.unnumbered}

By now, you can write, render and share a Quarto document in the format of your choice.
This part is about mastering Quarto.
Each chapter takes one core aspect of Quarto---Markdown, Figures and tables, Projects, Websites, Options and Troubleshooting---and gives you a deeper understanding of how it works.
That understanding helps you use Quarto more productively, find your way around the Quarto documentation, and solve problems on your own.

## Mastering your content

In @sec-writing you took a quick tour of the markdown you write in a `.qmd`, and the format chapters showed you what that content looks like in HTML, Typst and Revealjs.
The first three chapters help you master that content:

- @sec-authoring covers Quarto markdown in full, from text formatting and lists to equations, cross-references, citations and footnotes.
- @sec-figure-table and @sec-figure-table-computational are a pair.
  The first covers what applies to every figure and table: captions, cross-references and layout.
  The second covers figures and tables produced by code cells, such as their size, format and resolution.

## Mastering projects

A project is a folder of documents that Quarto treats as a whole.
Projects let you share options across documents, render them together, and control where the output goes.
Websites are one kind of project:

- @sec-projects shows you how to organize, configure and render a Quarto project.
- @sec-websites builds on projects to turn that folder into a website, with navigation, a theme and a place to publish it.

## Mastering how Quarto works

The next two chapters are less about particular features and more about the understanding that helps you use all of them:

- @sec-yaml builds on @sec-options.
  You'll learn how to find the option you need, where to put it, and how to get the YAML right.
- @sec-troubleshooting explains what Quarto does when you render a document, and uses that to help you track down problems.

## Beyond this book

No book can cover all of Quarto.
@sec-doing-more closes the book with the features we didn't cover, such as extensions, other formats and project types, and interactivity.
It tells you when you might want them and where to learn more.

## How to read this part

Unlike Getting Started, you don't need to read this part in order.
Read @sec-projects before @sec-websites and @sec-yaml, since both rely on how projects work.
Read @sec-figure-table before @sec-figure-table-computational.
Otherwise, read the chapters in any order, or come back to them as a reference when you need them.
